extracted.intended_audience: students, readers, and critics of literature; poets and writers interested in modern European literary standards
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and critical principles for judging or producing modern (19th-century) poetry and prose, with attention to originality, application of ideas, form, tone, and cultural influence. Emphasises the 'modern spirit' as applied by figures like Goethe and Heine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work from within outwards (artist's individuality)
rubrics_metrics.description: "As man must live from within outwards, so the artist must work from within outwards, ... he can only bring to light his own individuality."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality is produced by expressing the artist's inner individuality rather than conforming to external prescriptions or accepted authorities. Anti-pattern: following routine thinking or external standards ('such a thing must be so' because of authority). Example: Goethe's injunction to put the standard inside every man ('But _is_ it so? is it so to _me_?').

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality = individuality, not mere novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality consists in the revelation of one's own individuality, producing a 'poetry of nature' rather than artificial contrivance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek forms and subjects that allow the writer's individual voice to appear. Avoid contrivance that prioritizes novelty over authentic personal vision. The page emphasizes that even when attempting contortions, the artist reveals himself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply modern ideas to life (practical application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Literature should not hoard ideas as 'gold-nuggets' to be played with; rather, modern ideas must be applied freely and practically in literature and life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuing applied ideas over mere intellectual ornament: Heine's mission was to show ideas applied with freedom, clearness, and originality. Anti-pattern: treating ideas as counters or marbles, leading to slack, powerless culture (German writers who 'play' with ideas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resistance to Philistinism (valuing ideas over mere practical convenience)
rubrics_metrics.description: A writer should oppose 'Philistinism' — the complacent valorisation of mere practical convenience and respectability at the expense of ideas and reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The critic should value reason and the idea 'irrespectively of the practical conveniences' they may bring. Anti-pattern: literary culture dominated by practicality and precedent without appeal to general principles (the 'genuine British narrowness').

rubrics_metrics.name: Blend clearness, lightness, and freedom with power of feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective modern writing combines 'wonderful clearness, lightness, and freedom' with strong feeling and wide range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emulate Heine's combination of French modern clarity and German sentiment: lucid, nimble expression that still carries depth of emotion and wide intellectual reach. Example: Heine's use of both wit and pathos in prose and verse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unite wit and pathos
rubrics_metrics.description: A powerful literary voice often mingles wit with seriousness and pathos, rendering criticism and sentiment more effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heine is praised for 'so much wit with so much pathos' which makes him an effective writer. Guidance: deploy humor and ironic observation alongside genuine feeling to intensify impact; avoid one-note demeanors (purely sardonic or purely sentimental).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriate poetic form and musical rhythm
rubrics_metrics.description: Mastery of poetical form (e.g., popular ballad-forms) and rhythm contributes to poetic pleasure and expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heine's use of an old German popular ballad-form provides rapidity, grace, fulness, and pathos. Guidance: choose forms that suit voice and subject and handle them with lightness and ease. Anti-pattern: awkward or inappropriate rhythms (the text contrasts beautiful German rhythm with awkward French attempts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remain contemporary in voice when treating historical subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: When adopting historical or foreign subjects, the writer should not become anachronistically 'beautifully objective' (hubsch objektiv); instead retain the modern, personal tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heine treats varied historical figures but 'always remains Heinrich Heine, a son of the nineteenth century.' Guidance: avoid complete impersonation of past epochs; let contemporary perspective and authorial identity carry the piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticism should value synthesis and cultural junctions
rubrics_metrics.description: One important measure of literary value is the ability to synthesize influences (e.g., joining the French spirit to German ideas) producing something new and widely influential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heine's merit is in creating a junction between French clarity/practicality and German intellectual depth; critics should assess works for their cultural and intellectual synthesis, not just local originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernism: reject stock classicism and romanticism where they constrain thought
rubrics_metrics.description: True modernism resists stock classicism and stock romanticism, applying the modern point of view across subjects rather than nostalgically reviving old periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid literature that merely continues an old period until it expires; instead apply current ideas and critical perspective across themes. Anti-pattern: writers absorbed in Middle-Age revivalism to the point of losing modern relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate influence by practical cultural effect, not only literary scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: The value of a writer can be measured by the practical effect of their writing on national culture (e.g., liberating minds, affecting public taste), not just aesthetic qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay notes Goethe's slow but deep liberation and Heine's propagation of ideas that changed cultural sympathies. Guidance: in assessment, consider a work's capacity to alter public thought or sensibility over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid treating intellectual riches as mere display
rubrics_metrics.description: A writer should not display abundant ideas merely for show; ideas must be engaged with and applied, otherwise they are like 'gold-nuggets' used as marbles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text warns that German literature sometimes teems with ideas that are not practically applied; good writing turns ideas into lived insight. Anti-pattern: erudition without direction, leading to slack and powerless literature.
